_note: Where-to-stay neighborhood/area guides for cities beyond Seoul/Busan/Jeju (which live in the STAY literal in build-seo.cjs). Same record shape as STAY: {city, kr, areas:[[areaName, whyDescription], ...]}. Area entries describe DISTRICTS/NEIGHBORHOODS only — NO hotel/brand names. Descriptions are general, verifiable orientation facts (who it suits, transit access, atmosphere), hedged where appropriate. City keys match city-l10n.json exactly; kr labels taken from city-l10n.json.

areas: Songdo
Modern comfort & families — a planned waterfront district with wide parks, malls and convention centers; calm and spacious, though a subway or bus ride from the old city sights.
Wolmido / Open Port (Jung-gu)
Sightseeing & atmosphere — close to Chinatown, the historic open-port streets and the seaside promenade; walkable and characterful, handy for ferries to nearby islands.
Near Incheon Airport (Yeongjong)
Layovers & early flights — convenient for transit travelers who want to be minutes from the terminals; quieter and less central for general city exploring.
Bomun Lake Resort area
Resorts & relaxation — a landscaped lakeside zone east of the center with larger hotels and spas; scenic and quiet, but you'll want a bus or taxi to reach the historic core.
Hwangnidan-gil / Historic Center
First-timers & walkers — beside the royal tombs, Cheomseongdae and the trendy Hwangnidan-gil cafe street; central and atmosphere-rich, ideal for exploring on foot.
Near Singyeongju KTX Station
Train arrivals & convenience — practical if you arrive by KTX and want an easy base, though it sits outside town and generally needs a bus or taxi into the sights.
Hanok Village (Pungnam-dong)
Tradition & first-timers — staying in or beside the famous hanok village puts you among traditional guesthouses, food alleys and landmarks; central and immersive, can be busy on weekends.
Gaeksa / Downtown
Shopping & nightlife — the modern downtown around Gaeksa has shops, restaurants and bars within walking distance of the hanok area; lively and convenient.
Near Jeonju Station / Express Bus Terminal
Transit convenience — handy for arrivals and departures, generally cheaper, but a short bus or taxi ride from the main attractions.
Dongseongno / Jung-gu (Downtown)
First-timers & shopping — the central downtown core with the Dongseongno shopping street, markets and dense dining; very walkable with strong subway access.
Near Dongdaegu Station
Train travelers & connections — beside the KTX/express-bus hub, making intercity trips easy; practical and well-connected, a little less atmospheric than downtown.
Suseong-gu
Quiet & upscale comfort — a calmer residential-leaning area around Suseong Lake with parks and restaurants; relaxed, better suited to travelers wanting space over nightlife.
Near Daejeon Station / Jung-gu
Train hubs & convenience — central and tied to the main KTX station, with traditional markets and eateries nearby; practical for travelers using Daejeon as a transit base.
Dunsan / Seo-gu
Modern comfort & dining — the newer business and government district with department stores, restaurants and broad streets; clean and convenient, popular for longer or business stays.
Yuseong
Hot springs & relaxation — known for its spa and hot-spring tradition, suiting travelers who want a restful, wellness-oriented base away from the busiest streets.
Sokcho Beach & Expo area
Beach & first-timers — close to the long sandy beach and waterfront; scenic and relaxed in summer, an easy base for seaside time.
Jungang Market / Downtown
Food & convenience — beside the lively Jungang traditional market and the harbor, with abundant seafood; central and walkable for dining and day-trip planning.
Near Seoraksan / Daepo Port
Hikers & nature — closer to Seoraksan National Park access or the fishing-port atmosphere of Daepo; better for travelers prioritizing the mountains or fresh seafood over the town center.
Gyeongpo Beach & Lake
Beach & resorts — around the wide Gyeongpo beach and lake with cafes and seaside hotels; scenic and relaxed, the classic summer base, busier in peak season.
Anmok Beach (Coffee Street)
Cafes & atmosphere — the seafront cafe district popular for sea-view coffee and sunrises; laid-back and walkable, well-suited to leisurely stays.
Near Gangneung KTX Station / Downtown
Train arrivals & convenience — handy for the fast train from Seoul and close to markets and downtown dining; practical, with beaches a short bus or taxi away.
Dolsan / Night-view waterfront
Scenery & first-timers — near the famous illuminated harbor, Dolsan Bridge and the cable car; celebrated for night views, ideal for travelers chasing the coastal scenery.
Expo / Odongdo area
Sights & families — beside the Expo waterfront and Odongdo island with promenades and attractions; convenient and pleasant for sightseeing on foot.
Near Yeosu-Expo Station / Downtown
Transit & dining — close to the KTX station and central seafood restaurants and markets; practical for arrivals and food-focused stays.
Hwaseong Fortress / Haenggung-dong
History & first-timers — beside the UNESCO-listed Hwaseong Fortress and the atmospheric Haenggung-dong cafe and gallery streets; walkable and rich in sights.
Suwon Station area
Transit & shopping — around the major rail hub with department stores, malls and dense dining; very convenient for connections and a common, well-priced base.
Yeongtong / Gwanggyo
Modern & quiet comfort — newer districts with parks, lakeside areas and clean streets; calmer and more spread out, better for space than central buzz.
Hahoe Folk Village area
Tradition & immersion — staying near the historic Hahoe village offers traditional hanok lodging and a heritage atmosphere; tranquil and scenic, but well outside the city center.
Downtown Andong
Convenience & food — the central area with markets, the famous Andong jjimdak restaurants and everyday amenities; practical and walkable as a base for exploring the region.
Near Andong Station
Transit convenience — handy for train and bus arrivals and generally simpler for getting around the wider area; a functional base rather than a scenic one.
Gangguan Port / Jungang Market
First-timers & food — the lively central harbor beside Jungang Market, ferry terminals and the cable car; walkable and atmospheric, with abundant seafood.
Dongpirang Village area
Atmosphere & views — near the colorful mural village on the hill above the port; charming and photogenic, with stair-heavy lanes and harbor views.
Near Tongyeong Bus Terminal
Transit convenience — practical for intercity bus arrivals and generally quieter and cheaper, a short ride from the waterfront sights.
Myeongdong / Downtown (Dakgalbi Street)
First-timers & food — the central area with the famous dakgalbi alley, shops and nightlife; walkable and convenient as a main base.
Near Chuncheon / Namchuncheon Station
Transit & day trips — close to the ITX rail line from Seoul, easy for arrivals and excursions; practical and well-connected.
Soyang River / Lakeside
Scenery & relaxation — toward the rivers and lakes with rail-bike, ferries and Nami Island access; calmer and more scenic, suited to nature-focused stays.
Yeongildae Beach
Beach & first-timers — around the city's main urban beach and seaside promenade; convenient and lively in summer, an easy coastal base close to downtown.
Jukdo Market / Downtown
Food & convenience — beside the large Jukdo seafood market and central dining; practical and walkable for travelers focused on food and city access.
Homigot area
Sunrises & scenery — toward the easterly cape known for sunrise views; scenic but well outside the center, better for a short scenic stay than a main base.
Mokpo Modern History / Waterfront
Sights & first-timers — near the old open-port streets, Yudalsan and the harbor with the marine cable car; characterful and walkable for sightseeing.
Near Mokpo Station / Downtown
Transit & convenience — beside the KTX terminus with markets and dining nearby; practical for arrivals and island-ferry connections.
Pyeonghwa Square / Dancing Sea Fountain area
Evening atmosphere — along the newer waterfront with the seafront fountain show and restaurants; pleasant for relaxed seaside evenings.
Near Suncheonman Bay / Garden Expo
Nature & first-timers — toward the famous coastal wetland reserve and the National Garden; scenic and spacious, ideal for travelers centered on the gardens and bay.
Downtown Suncheon / Station area
Convenience & transit — the central area near the rail station with markets, dining and everyday amenities; practical and well-connected as a base.
Naganeupseong area
Tradition & quiet — near the historic walled folk village outside town; heritage-rich and tranquil, but removed from city conveniences.
